title: Authorization matrix reconciliation and audit pipeline hardening
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need to reconcile the new RBAC v2 authorization graph with the admin console and harden the audit forwarding pipeline after the recent pentest uncovered gaps in role inheritance, assertion validation for SAML SSO, and missing immutable audit trails for privileged actions. This ticket drives the remediation plan: code fixes, tests, deployment strategy, and validation checks for the console and private deployment stacks.

Scope and goals:
- Validate RBAC v2 graph generation end-to-end (policy -> compiled grants -> enforcement) across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Implement targeted fixes for pen-test findings: weak admin-exception routing, role escalation via compound RBAC paths, and missing assertion binding checks in SAML connector.
- Harden audit-forwarding: ensure immutable event IDs, signed event envelopes, and guaranteed delivery to customer-configured destinations (Splunk/Datadog/Customer Kinesis).
- Add runtime assertions and CI checks: graph diff tests, SAML assertion schema validation, and audit ingestion blackbox tests.
- Plan canary rollback and monitoring for any policy-enforcement changes to avoid customer lockout.

Deliverables:
1) RBAC graph validation harness (unit + integration): deterministic reconciliation tool that flags unexpected grants and generates remediation patches.
2) SAML connector hardening: stricter audience/recipient checks, enforce InResponseTo when present, and reject unsigned assertions per policy.
3) Audit pipeline changes: event signing, retry+DLQ semantics, and an audit-forwarding observability dashboard with per-tenant delivery SLO.
4) Runbook for admin recovery (safety net to recover locked orgs).
5) PRs, design doc, and test matrix for security review.

Technical approach and trade-offs:
- RBAC reconciliation will use a graph diff approach rather than rewriting the policy compiler. Pros: limited blast radius, easier to prove fixes. Cons: must ensure diffs don't miss runtime-transient grants (eg. delegated sessions).
- Audit signing uses HMAC with tenant-specific keys stored in KMS. We debated JWT-like envelopes but chose compact HMAC envelopes to minimize latency on high-throughput audit paths.
- SAML strictness: enabling full strict checks now increases false-positive risk for some older customers. We'll gate strict mode behind a feature flag with an opt-in grace period and telemetry to identify impacted orgs.

Status and recent progress (summary of notes):
- 2026-03-02: Triage meeting. Owners assigned. Initial pen-test report linked. Agreed P0 for fixes affecting admin escalation.
- 2026-03-04: RBAC reconciliation PoC written (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/security/rbac-recon). PoC discovers 3 non-trivial inheritance paths in staging causing elevated read-access.
- 2026-03-06: SAML connector PR (GH#4102) created with audience/recipient checks. Blocked by failing integration tests against legacy IdP fixtures.
- 2026-03-08: Audit signing design reviewed with infra and ops. Decision: HMAC per-tenant key, sign at ingestion layer, verify at forwarder and on storage side.
- 2026-03-10: Added graph-diff CI job; initial run flagged two regressions introduced by recent console change.
- 2026-03-11: Security review prep started; drafting threat-model addendum focusing on admin path attack surfaces (delegation, session token reuse, parameter-based RBAC overrides).

Open tasks (next 2 sprints):
- Complete SAML integration tests with updated IdP fixtures (owner: Rafael; estimate: 2 pts).
- Finalize RBAC reconciliation tool and add auto-remediation option behind feature flag (owner: Matthew Li; estimate: 3 pts).
- Implement audit HMAC signing and DLQ semantics; add observability (owner: Infra team; estimate: 3 pts).
- Create and validate admin recovery runbook and automated escape hatch endpoints (owner: SRE; estimate: 2 pts).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Strict SAML enforcement may break older customer IdPs. Mitigation: staged opt-in flag + telemetry + support playbook.
- Risk: RBAC graph fixes could inadvertently remove legitimate grants. Mitigation: graph-diff dry-run mode + canary rollout + explicit approval step in console for remediation patches.
- Risk: Audit pipeline performance regression due to signing. Mitigation: microbenchmarks, use native crypto libraries, and add sampling for very high-throughput routes.

Notes / Links:
- Pen-test report (internal): https://drive.redwood.company/security/pen-test-2026/rbac-sso-audit-findings.pdf
- RBAC recon PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/tree/main/rbac-recon
- SAML connector PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity/pull/4102
- Audit design doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/Sec/Audit+Signing+Design

Acceptance criteria:
- All critical pen-test findings verified closed in staging and validated by security engineering.
- RBAC reconciliation runs in CI and blocks merges that introduce unexpected grants.
- SAML connector rejects malformed/unsigned assertions by default, with opt-in relaxation documented.
- Audit pipeline produces signed, verifiable events, with monitored delivery SLO and documented recovery steps.

Outreach and review plan:
- Schedule security review with applied ML and infra on 2026-03-16.
- Coordinate with solutions engineering for any customer-facing changes during grace period for SAML tightening.
